{{Short description|Geometric object}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Uniform ''k''<sub>&hairsp;21</sub> polytope}}
In [[geometry]], a '''uniform ''k''<sub>21</sub> polytope''' is a [[polytope]] in ''k''&nbsp;+&nbsp;4 dimensions constructed from the [[En (Lie algebra)|''E''<sub>''n''</sub>]] [[Coxeter group]], and having only [[regular polytope]] facets. The family was named by their [[Coxeter symbol]] '''''k''<sub>21</sub>''' by its bifurcating [[Coxeter–Dynkin diagram]], with a single ring on the end of the ''k''-node sequence.

[[Thorold Gosset]] discovered this family as a part of his 1900 enumeration of the [[regular polytope|regular]] and [[semiregular polytope]]s, and so they are sometimes called '''Gosset's semiregular figures'''. Gosset named them by their dimension from 5 to 9, for example the ''5-ic semiregular figure''.

== Family members ==
The sequence as identified by Gosset ends as an infinite tessellation (space-filling honeycomb) in 8-space, called the [[E8 lattice]]. (A final form was not discovered by Gosset and is called the '''E9 lattice''': 6<sub>21</sub>. It is a tessellation of hyperbolic 9-space constructed of ∞ 9-[[simplex]] and ∞ 9-[[orthoplex]] facets with all vertices at infinity.)

The family starts uniquely as [[6-polytope]]s. The ''triangular prism'' and ''rectified 5-cell'' are included at the beginning for completeness. The ''demipenteract'' also exists in the [[demihypercube]] family.

They are also sometimes named by their symmetry group, like '''E6 polytope''', although there are many [[uniform polytope]]s within the [[E6 (mathematics)|''E''<sub>6</sub>]] symmetry.

The complete family of Gosset semiregular polytopes are:
# [[triangular prism]]: −1<sub>21</sub> (2 [[triangle]]s and 3 [[Square (geometry)|square]] faces)
# [[rectified 5-cell]]: 0<sub>21</sub>, ''Tetroctahedric'' (5 [[Tetrahedron|tetrahedra]] and 5 [[Octahedron|octahedra]] cells)
# [[demipenteract]]: 1<sub>21</sub>, ''5-ic semiregular figure'' (16 [[5-cell]] and 10 [[16-cell]] facets)
# [[2 21 polytope]]: 2<sub>21</sub>, ''6-ic semiregular figure'' (72 5-[[simplex]] and 27 5-[[orthoplex]] facets)
# [[3 21 polytope]]: 3<sub>21</sub>, ''7-ic semiregular figure'' (576 6-[[simplex]] and 126 6-[[orthoplex]] facets)
# [[4 21 polytope]]: 4<sub>21</sub>, ''8-ic semiregular figure'' (17280 7-[[simplex]] and 2160 7-[[orthoplex]] facets)
# [[5 21 honeycomb]]: 5<sub>21</sub>, ''9-ic semiregular check'' tessellates Euclidean 8-space (∞ 8-[[simplex]] and ∞ 8-[[orthoplex]] facets)
# [[6 21 honeycomb]]: 6<sub>21</sub>, tessellates hyperbolic 9-space (∞ 9-[[simplex]] and ∞ 9-[[orthoplex]] facets)

Each polytope is constructed from (''n''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1)-[[simplex]] and (''n''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1)-[[orthoplex]] facets.

The orthoplex faces are constructed from the [[Coxeter group]] ''D''<sub>''n''&minus;1</sub> and have a [[Schläfli symbol]] of {3<sup>1,''n''&minus;1,1</sup>} rather than the regular {3<sup>''n''&minus;2</sup>,4}. This construction is an implication of two "facet types". Half the facets around each orthoplex [[Ridge (geometry)|ridge]] are attached to another orthoplex, and the others are attached to a simplex. In contrast, every simplex ridge is attached to an orthoplex.

Each has a [[vertex figure]] as the previous form. For example, the ''rectified 5-cell'' has a vertex figure as a ''triangular prism''.
